note: Drafted by research-agent on 2026-11-12 and revised the same day after research review 001. Every entry is DERIVED unless marked STATED. Rules are cited as capability/BR id (for example L1-accounts/BR-006), because BR ids restart in each capability. Baseline decisions cite the human gate record (.mw/runs/BASELINE-2026-10-30/baseline-review-report.json). Owners come from research/inputs/decision-makers.md, which is a DEMO ASSUMPTION naming kurtis in every role.

entries.title: The 80 live baseline rules describe all externally observable behaviour of minidon
entries.description: Parity is defined as 'every live baseline rule has a passing parity test'. That is only equal to feature parity if the rules cover every observable behaviour. The baseline maps 71.0% of code to capabilities; the unmapped 29% includes shared infrastructure with observable effects (minidon/main.py DomainError handler, minidon/deps.py auth dependencies, FastAPI/Pydantic request validation, the /openapi.json, /docs and /redoc routes, the 404 and 405 bodies). Behaviour there is not captured as a business rule. Tested by the differential check in falsifiedIf.

entries.title: A Rust build can read and write the existing SQLite data byte-compatibly without a migration
entries.description: The ticket requires same data, no migration. Python stores data through SQLAlchemy on SQLite (minidon/db.py, default sqlite:///./minidon.db). Observed by the reviewer's probe of the Python reference on a fresh database (research-review-001 F-09): enum columns (Role, Visibility, NotificationKind, ReportCategory, ReportState) store the enum member NAME, for example accounts.role = 'ADMIN' and statuses.visibility = 'PRIVATE', while the API returns the value ('admin', 'private'); the DDL sizes enum columns to the longest name (role VARCHAR(9)); datetimes are stored as naive UTC text 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff' and serialised by the API as naive ISO 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffff' with no zone. Password hashes are '<salt hex>$<digest hex>' and access tokens (secrets.token_urlsafe(32), 43 characters, column String(64)) are the primary key. The assumption is that every one of these can be reproduced exactly in Rust.

entries.title: Parity can be proven black-box at the HTTP boundary, with the Python build as the oracle
entries.description: The Python repository stays unchanged and serves as the reference (ticket.md). The assumption is that both builds can be run against copies of the same database with controlled data timestamps, so each parity test can assert the same status code and response body for the same request. The existing Python tests are in-process (dependency_overrides, monkeypatched utcnow), so they are a guide, not the harness (MET-003).

entries.title: The baseline gate decisions stand for the length of the rebuild
entries.description: The 7 conflict resolutions and 21 open-question answers recorded by kurtis at the baseline gate (2026-11-09 and 2026-11-10, .mw/runs/BASELINE-2026-10-30/baseline-review-report.json) define what 'current behaviour' means: copy the code, keep the known weaknesses, record the follow-ups. The answers are a human statement (STATED); the assumption that nobody reverses one before 2027-03-31 is DERIVED. If one is reversed, the parity target for the affected rules changes.

Per the rules-trace indexes (research/inputs/baseline-metrics.md), 64 of the 81 rules are DERIVED or STATED/DERIVED and 17 are purely STATED: L1-accounts 12 of 14 DERIVED or mixed, L1-following 11 of 15, L1-posting 16 of 20, L1-timelines 6 of 8, L1-notifications 7 of 9, L1-moderation 12 of 15. The purely STATED 17 are L1-accounts/BR-001, BR-009; L1-following/BR-001, BR-002, BR-010, BR-011; L1-posting/BR-001, BR-004, BR-007, BR-009 (retired); L1-timelines/BR-001, BR-005; L1-notifications/BR-001, BR-005; L1-moderation/BR-001, BR-005, BR-009. Decision (STATED, research/inputs/human-decisions.md ## 4): the L0-minidon domain sign-off at the baseline gate on 2026-11-10 is treated as human confirmation of the DERIVED rules, so none is unconfirmed. Parity tests check what the Python code does, so this does not change the test approach. Caveat (DERIVED): the sign-off was a single domain-level approval by one DEMO reviewer, not a rule-by-rule review.

entries.title: A baseline gate decision is reversed during the rebuild
entries.description: The gate answers are human decisions, but they were all made by one DEMO reviewer (RISK-007). If a real BA, Tech Lead or Security reviewer reverses one, a parity rule becomes a behaviour change, which is out of scope for this ticket and would need its own ticket or a scope change at the research gate.

entries.title: Silent data incompatibility in stored formats
entries.description: Known formats (observed in the reviewer's probe, research-review-001 F-09): enum columns store the member NAME in upper case ('ADMIN', 'PRIVATE'), not the StrEnum value the API returns; datetimes are naive UTC text 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff'; enum columns are VARCHAR sized to the longest name. Other failure points: boolean and NULL handling, integer id sequences, and the PBKDF2 hash string format. A mismatch may not fail loudly: Rust could misread rows or write rows that Python later misreads. Mitigation: round-trip tests in both directions on a copy of a Python-created database (NFR-002), and matching DDL if Rust ever creates the schema (NFR-011).

entries.title: Framework behaviour that is observable but not a business rule
entries.description: FastAPI and Pydantic decide request validation errors (a 422 body {"detail": [...]}, different from the DomainError 422 body {"error": msg}), JSON serialisation (naive ISO datetimes, nulls, field order), default status codes, trailing-slash redirects, unknown routes ({"detail": "Not Found"}), 405 handling and the /openapi.json, /docs and /redoc routes. None of this is in the 80 live rules, but API clients can depend on it. If it is not specified, Rust will differ. Mitigation: a differential test over all 40 endpoints, plus a design decision on which framework behaviours are part of the contract (ADR candidate 3).

entries.title: About 31 of 81 rules have no existing Python test
entries.description: Rough measure (DERIVED, grep of ### BR- sections in .mw/context/capabilities/*/rules-trace.md for a tests/test_*.py reference, 2026-11-12): about 50 of the 81 rule sections cite an existing Python test (L1-accounts 5 of 14, L1-following 9 of 15, L1-posting 13 of 20, L1-timelines 7 of 8, L1-notifications 5 of 9, L1-moderation 11 of 15). So about 31 parity tests have to be written from the rules-trace alone and checked against the Python build first, which adds work and the chance that a test encodes a misread rule. A citation is not proof that the test asserts the rule; planning should confirm per rule.

entries.title: The reason for moving to Rust is unstated, and performance is not measured
entries.description: The ticket says 'Move minidon from Python to Rust' but gives no business reason, and performance parity is not required. The human decisions of 2026-11-12 (research/inputs/human-decisions.md ## 5) record the reason as still open, for the PO to supply. If the real motive is performance, cost or safety, nothing in this pack measures it, and there is no Python latency or throughput baseline to compare with later. Recommendation: the PO states the reason at the research gate, or adds a performance metric and has the Python version measured first. This pack does not guess a reason.

entries.title: Known security weaknesses are carried forward on purpose
entries.description: Parity keeps PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 100,000 iterations (below the OWASP figure of 600,000 or more), an 8-character minimum password, access tokens stored in clear text as the database key, first-registrant-becomes-Admin (L1-accounts/BR-006) and staff deletes with no audit trail (L1-posting/BR-013). The baseline gate accepted these and named follow-ups for each (OQ-001, OQ-002, OQ-003, OQ-009); human-decisions.md ## 3 puts them out of scope for this lift and shift. They must be raised as follow-up tickets so they are not forgotten. See security.md.

entries.title: One person holds every decision and review role
entries.description: decision-makers.md is a DEMO ASSUMPTION naming kurtis as PO, BA, Tech Lead, Security reviewer and gate approver; the baseline gate answers and human-decisions.md come from the same person. Agents keep I-14 among themselves, but there is no independent human review of the domain, architecture and security lanes. Replace with real people before relying on the pack.

entries.title: Time-dependent rules are hard to compare across two builds
entries.description: The 60-minute edit window, the 30-posts-per-rolling-hour rate limit, the 30-day token TTL and created_at ordering all read the wall clock (minidon/db.py utcnow). Parity tests need the same controllable time in both builds, or they will flake. The Python build has no clock injection point outside its in-process tests and must not be changed, so black-box tests set data timestamps in the shared database file instead of the clock.

entries.title: Concurrency behaviour may differ under an async Rust runtime
entries.description: Python opens SQLite with check_same_thread False and one session per request. A Rust build with a connection pool and concurrent writers may hit 'database is locked' errors the Python build does not, and the COUNT(*)-based first-registrant-becomes-Admin check (L1-accounts/BR-006) has a race that may play out differently. Parity tests are sequential, so they will not catch this.

entries.title: Python and Rust text semantics differ even when the logic is translated faithfully
entries.description: Regex dialect: MENTION_PATTERN and HASHTAG_PATTERN (minidon/statuses/service.py:19-20) use negative lookbehind ((?<![\w@]), (?<![\w#])) and \b; the standard Rust regex crate has no lookaround, and Python's \w and \b are Unicode-aware. These patterns decide mentions, hashtags, mention notifications and who can see direct and private statuses (service.py:46-51), so a mismatch is also a disclosure risk (security.md row 4). String length: Python len() counts code points; limits use it at statuses/service.py:229 (500, including the spoiler text), accounts/service.py:45, 122, 126 and moderation/service.py:28; Rust str::len() counts bytes. Case and whitespace: Python's Unicode str.lower() (usernames, emails, tags) and str.strip() (content, email) differ from Rust's ASCII-only helpers. Token shape: secrets.token_urlsafe(32) gives 43 URL-safe characters in a String(64) column. Mitigation: NFR-010 and GRD-009, with non-ASCII inputs as a required parity-test class.

entries.description: Decided by kurtis at the baseline gate (baseline-review-report.json, 2026-11-09), so no longer deferred to design: L1-accounts owns get_by_username as a stable identity-resolution API whose changes need review by consuming capabilities (CF-004, closes OQ-018); Moderation calls Posting's soft delete directly and the boost cascade is intended (CF-006, closes OQ-017); social/queries.py stays a plain import owned by L1-following, not a formal contract (CF-003, closes OQ-005). Design decides only how these look in Rust. Lists is removed (CF-002, closes OQ-020 and OQ-021). Password hashing (OQ-003) is a follow-up outside this rebuild.

entries.title: A representative existing dataset for compatibility testing
entries.description: 'Same data' needs a real or realistic SQLite database created by the Python build. No dataset is named in the inputs. Without one, compatibility tests use a database the tests build through the Python API, which may miss legacy rows.
